author: Avery
text: Can we use this thread to do a quick final pass on the dashboard demo?

author: Mina
text: Yes. I think we should start with the upload flow because it is the easiest feature to understand.

author: Diego
text: After upload, we can switch to the thread map and expand the conversation so the structure is obvious.

author: Noor
text: Let's keep the explanation short there. The visual already does a lot of the work.

author: Theo
text: Agreed. We should show expand, collapse, then filter by one topic.

author: Jules
text: I can prepare the short narration for the topic filter section.

author: Rina
text: Should we mention the sentiment footer before or after filtering?

author: Avery
text: After filtering. That way the audience sees the summary update based on visible messages.

author: Mina
text: Good point. The footer is stronger when it reacts to something we just changed.

author: Diego
text: We should include one critical or mixed message in the dataset so the sentiment display is not one-note.

author: Noor
text: That is realistic. Most team conversations have a few concerns, even when the overall tone is positive.

author: Theo
text: I tested the JSON upload with a small file. It showed up in the dataset selector right away.

author: Jules
text: Did the parent-child links render correctly in the map?

author: Theo
text: Yes. The roots appeared as topic cards, and replies expanded in the right order.

author: Rina
text: Let's keep this sample file clean so nothing distracts from the upload feature.

author: Avery
text: Exactly. No missing parents, no duplicate ids, and timestamps should be in a natural order.

author: Mina
text: For the phone demo, we should load the page once on the laptop first so everything is cached.

author: Diego
text: That should make the classroom demo smoother, especially if the network is slow.

author: Noor
text: I will bring a backup screenshot just in case the projector connection gives us trouble.

author: Theo
text: Good idea. We probably will not need it, but it is nice to have.

author: Jules
text: Can someone confirm the final speaking order?

author: Avery
text: I will introduce the problem, Mina can demo upload, Diego can show the map, and Noor can close with takeaways.

author: Rina
text: The current map controls feel ready. Expand and fullscreen both make the demo easier to follow.

author: Mina
text: I like that fullscreen keeps the topic selector visible. It feels much better for presenting.

author: Diego
text: The one thing to watch is graph density when every branch is expanded.

author: Noor
text: We can solve that by expanding all briefly, then collapsing and opening one branch.

author: Theo
text: That gives the audience both the overview and the detail view.

author: Jules
text: I think we are ready. The flow now feels simple enough for a quick showcase.

author: Avery
text: Great. Let's rehearse once with the short file and once with the larger file.

author: Rina
text: Sounds good. I will time each section so we do not run over.
